assumptions_not_known: does not trust marketing claims of security
evaluates defense-in-depth from an assume-breach posture
inspects every unauthenticated parser and endpoint

criteria.name: input handling
criteria.evidence: backend/app/services/ingestion.py: Bleach allowlist sanitizes raw HTML; RFC 5322 MIME parser wrapped in try/except; 25MB file size cap enforced.
criteria.quote: Robust input filtering on email ingestion path with defense against malicious HTML/XSS payloads.

criteria.name: authn-authz
criteria.evidence: Platform is structured as an air-gapped forensic appliance without active multi-user session auth on local API endpoints.
criteria.quote: Single-tenant appliance model acceptable for demo freeze; enterprise multi-tenant RBAC remains a roadmap requirement.

criteria.name: secrets
criteria.evidence: backend/app/config.py: Hardcoded demo keys guarded by ENVIRONMENT production check; documented allowlist in SECURITY.md.
criteria.quote: Clear separation between air-gapped demo defaults and production runtime requirements.

criteria.name: dependency posture
criteria.evidence: frontend npm audit reports 2 vulnerabilities in dev server dependencies (esbuild <=0.24.2 / Vite <=6.4.2); python dependencies clean.
criteria.quote: Frontend dev server dependencies require bump to Vite 6.4.3.

criteria.name: defense-in-depth
criteria.evidence: OWASP headers middleware injected on all responses (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff).
criteria.quote: Comprehensive HTTP response security headers implemented across all routes.

top_finding: Frontend dev-server dependency Vite 6.4.2 has known moderate/high advisory (GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99); requires bump to 6.4.3.
unanswered_question: Are API routes protected against CSRF if deployed in a cross-origin web browser context without custom authorization headers?
